title: AI tools for cool mobile game
author: Typical-Piano-2963
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I’m a software engineer with a web development background, and I want to create a simple Flutter mobile puzzle/math game. My main challenge is the visual side since I’m not a game designer.

I’m looking for AI tools (free if possible) that can help me generate:

* Attractive mobile game UI/UX
* Game assets and animations
* Modern, colorful, addictive-looking interfaces

The style I’m aiming for is inspired by games like Ludo, Duolingo, Clash Royale, and Candy Crush — very polished, fun, and eye-catching.

The gameplay itself is relatively simple, but I want the design quality to feel professional and engaging.

What AI tools, workflows, or platforms would you recommend for:

* UI generation
* Character/icon creation
* Animations
* Overall game art direction
* Maybe even AI-assisted game development

Would love recommendations from people who already built mobile games using AI tools.

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
For UI/UX specifically, you're honestly better off using Figma with reference screenshots from the games you mentioned and then implementing directly in Flutter. AI image generators aren't great at producing usable UI components since you need exact dimensions, tap targets, and scalable assets rather than a pretty picture of a screen.

For the actual game assets (characters, icons, backgrounds), the main challenge you'll hit with general purpose image generators (Midjourney, DALL-E, Nano banana, etc.) is transparency and animation. Mobile game assets need clean alpha channels, and most of those tools output flat JPGs or PNGs with baked-in backgrounds that you'll have to manually cut out. They also have no understanding of animation.

I built GameLabs Studio [https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co) that handles transparent asset generation and animation, consistent style across sets of icons/characters, and tileable/extendable/parallax backgrounds. Useful when you need a batch of assets that all feel like they belong in the same game. Might be worth checking out for the character and icon side of things.

https://i.redd.it/ix3bcalfzp3h1.gif

For art direction, pick 3-4 reference games, screenshot, and use that as your style guide image when prompting. Consistency matters more than any single asset looking amazing.
